propositions: The _CASCADING_EDGES table's one-eligible-status-per-edge design guarantees that a parent moves along the same edge as its child, but does not prevent all cases where a child reaches a state ahead of its parent (e.g., closed child reactivating to in_progress under an open parent, or blocked child resuming to in_progress under an open parent).

The store must maintain the invariant that no non-terminal-state ticket can be a child of a closed ticket, enforced jointly by the table's closed-source rows and the unconditional close guard in transition_close.py.

The blocked→in_progress state transition does not cascade despite the start-work gate firing on that edge; the gate and cascade answer different questions (is work starting vs. would this leave an eligible ancestor behind) and their disagreement requires documented reconciliation in the table and docs.

Section I4a's headline sentence 'A child never runs ahead of its parent in the lifecycle' overstates the guarantee and must be narrowed to what the enumerated edge table actually provides, with documented residuals.
The reactivation of a closed child to in_progress under an open parent is accepted documented-intended behaviour because only a closed parent is eligible on that edge.
No transition refused today should become permitted, the claim-status guard must remain untouched, and the _CASCADING_EDGES table rows must remain byte-identical.
